packetInstructions: Note the October 1, 2027 gate in product copy from day one.

Motion content, § 16-806(c)(1): the motion must state all of the movant's unsealed and unexpunged citations, arrests, charges, and convictions as reasonably known, the grounds for eligibility, and facts in support. If the motion does not comply, the movant has 30 days after notice to amend, or the motion is dismissed without prejudice.

Scope relief, § 16-806(h): the movant need not satisfy the waiting periods for all records and need not seek relief for every eligible record. Packets can be scoped to what the person actually wants cleared.

The prosecutor is not required to respond. Under § 16-806(d) the motion is served on the prosecutor, but the prosecutor need not respond unless the court orders it. Do not tell users to expect an opposition by default.

Repeat-motion limits: under § 16-806(i)(6), after a denial the court entertains a second motion no sooner than one year, and a third and final motion no sooner than one year after that. A temporary provision, § 16-806(i)(7), exempts motions dismissed between March 1, 2025 and July 14, 2025 from the one-year wait.

Completion of the sentence, § 16-801(2), is unconditional discharge from incarceration, commitment, probation, parole, or supervised release, whichever is latest, and nonpayment of fines, restitution, or other monetary assessments does not prevent completion.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

Where a hearing is requested it must be held within 90 days of filing, and the motion asks in the alternative that the matter be set for hearing within 90 days. There is no prosecutor objection window on this route; the 90 days is a deadline for holding a hearing, not a period for the prosecuting attorney to object.
The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition, and where relied on, the Georgia criminal history report and proof of sentence completion.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the relief restricts the felony charge only and does not reach the misdemeanour conviction.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.
The participant obtains and attaches the order vacating or reversing the conviction and the record showing the decision became final through completion of the appellate process.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. The packet must say that Georgia restriction reaches Georgia records only and does not touch the demanding state's records or the FBI Identity History Summary.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.
The packet must tell the participant to follow up at day 31, because the facility must restrict within 30 days of the request.
Offer this route as a standard follow-on step after the restriction and sealing routes. Restriction at GCIC and sealing at the clerk do not automatically reach the jail's own records.

The participant obtains and encloses proof that the offence is already restricted — the criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or the restricting order. Prior restriction is the statutory precondition of the request and is a required-before-submission item, not a condition of generating the request.

packetInstructions: The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the court shall order restriction and sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers must restrict within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order.
The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition showing the First Offender sentence as Exhibit A.

packetInstructions: The prosecuting attorney receives notice of the petition. Notice is not a request for consent, there is no advance-consent gate on this route, and the packet must not describe one.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

The packet must say that the court shall order sealing within 90 days of filing, that the clerk then seals every document in its custody within 60 days, and that the court shall also order law enforcement agencies, jails and detention centers to restrict, with 30 days to comply after they receive a copy.
The participant obtains and attaches the final disposition showing the First Offender sentence, and the discharge order where one was entered, as Exhibit A.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Iowa District Court for the county of the case. Rule 2.80(3) requires the application to be filed in the case where expungement is sought, not the county of residence. Separate cases require separate applications.

rules.filing: eFile through the Iowa Judicial Branch eFile System where the case is available there, otherwise file on paper at the county clerk of court office. The application is filed in the case where expungement is sought, so separate cases require separate applications.
rules.fees: No filing fee for the application itself was identified in the review. Treat the amount as unconfirmed until verified at build time.
rules.feeWaiver: Not applicable while no fee is identified. Unresolved.
rules.notice: The county attorney is the notice recipient and may file a confidential response within 20 days after service unless the court orders otherwise. The court may conduct a hearing but none is required.
rules.service: eFiling serves the county attorney automatically. Paper filers complete the certification of service and mail or hand deliver a copy to the county attorney of the county where the application is filed.
rules.participantSignature: Required, under penalty of perjury. The August 2024 forms permit a digitized signature per the Iowa Judicial Branch instructions, or printing and hand-signing. Election A is self-represented, election B is by attorney.

packetInstructions: Do not add a proposed order to any Iowa Rule 2.86 packet. No proposed order is filed, which differs from most jurisdictions.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: Statewide statute and statewide forms. K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) directs the petition to the district court.

rules.filing: File with the clerk of the district court, docketed in the original criminal action, with the Criminal Cover Sheet, and make the fee-waiver request in the same filing.
rules.fees: Docket fee $176 under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2), plus any non-judicial personnel charge, except that on a specialty court petition under (a)(3) the court may waive all or part of the docket fee. This is the only fee waiver in K.S.A. 21-6614.
rules.feeWaiver: The court may waive all or part of the docket fee imposed for filing a petition under K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3). The waiver is discretionary and must be asked for.
rules.notice: The court sets the hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecutor and the arresting law enforcement agency.
rules.service: The clerk sends the Notice of Hearing. The participant does not serve and does not sign the certificate.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition under penalty of perjury.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The court in which the person pled guilty or was sentenced (§ 610.130.1). This is the court of plea or sentence, which for an ordinance violation will often be a municipal division and for a state misdemeanor an associate circuit division. It is not the county of arrest and it is not a freely chosen circuit court.
authority: S.S. v. Mitchell, 289 S.W.3d 797 (Mo. App. E.D. 2009)

rules.filing: An application filed with the clerk of the court in which the participant pled guilty or was sentenced (§ 610.130.1). Whether that court opens a new case or accepts the application under the original case number is local practice and is confirmed with the clerk. No Office of the State Courts Administrator form exists for this section, so the application and proposed order are LegalEase-drafted against the statutory contents and the track carries a local-form override for any circuit or municipal division that publishes its own.
rules.fees: Not fixed by the section and county-variable. The participant confirms the filing fee and costs with the clerk of the court of plea before filing. No fee figure is published on this track. The participant separately pays for the driver record, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol search.
rules.feeWaiver: GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040 where the filing court accepts the statewide form. Municipal divisions vary, and the participant confirms with the clerk.
rules.notice: Not prescribed by § 610.130, which requires a hearing but names no notice recipients. In practice the respondents named in the application — the prosecuting or city attorney, the arresting agency, the Highway Patrol and the Department of Revenue — are the entities whose records the order would reach, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk how that court notices them. Whether the participant or the clerk gives notice is a local-practice question the packet does not answer for them.
rules.service: Not prescribed by the section. The packet includes a certificate of service the participant may complete if the clerk directs that the applicant serve the named respondents, and leaves it blank otherwise.
rules.participantSignature: The applicant signs the application beneath a declaration under penalty of perjury. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
rules.notarization: none prescribed by § 610.130. A declaration under penalty of perjury is used. Where a local court requires an acknowledgment before a notary the participant is told to ask the clerk.

packetInstructions: Once in a lifetime, and the warning goes above the signature block. § 610.130.3 entitles a person to only one expungement under the section and lets the director keep records sufficient to enforce the limit. There is no second application.

This section and § 610.140 do not overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. § 610.140.3(7) excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 and § 610.140.3(8) excludes intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally.

Relief is mandatory on the findings. § 610.130.2 says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the three conditions are met after hearing. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary, and a required hearing is not a reason to withhold the packet.

The definition of alcohol-related enforcement contact is reproduced verbatim from § 302.525.3 in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise answer from memory of convictions and miss an administrative suspension entirely.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.

manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets the hearing and supplies the details after filing.

manualCompletionItems.why: Firstness is the whole eligibility question and it is the participant's to swear to. The once-in-a-lifetime consequence makes a machine-generated guess unacceptable.

Every intoxication-related matter carries an attorney-review recommendation and a contested-hearing handoff on the face of the packet. The ten-year showing turns on a driver record most participants have never read, and getting it wrong spends the one lifetime application.

Relief is mandatory on the findings. § 610.130.2 says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the three conditions are met after hearing. The packet must not describe the outcome as discretionary, and a required hearing is not a reason to withhold the packet.

The definition of alcohol-related enforcement contact is reproduced verbatim from § 302.525.3 in the participant materials, because a participant asked whether they have had one will otherwise answer from memory of convictions and miss an administrative suspension entirely.

The Department of Revenue driver record, any out-of-state driver records, the certified docket and the Highway Patrol criminal record are obtained by the participant before filing. None of them delays generation.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It is the document that shows administrative suspensions and revocations under §§ 302.500 to 302.540 and chemical-test refusals, which are alcohol-related enforcement contacts under § 302.525.3 even where no conviction followed. A participant who answers the enforcement-contact question from memory will very often be wrong.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Out-of-state driver records. Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state, and § 610.130.4 bars anyone issued or required to hold a commercial driver's licence in any state.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The licensing authority of each other state where the participant has held a licence
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence in any state other than Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense." against Out-of-state driver records, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence in any state other than Missouri.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified docket sheet and judgment from the court of plea or sentence. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It establishes the plea or sentencing date the ten-year period runs from, the offense level, and the case number.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the municipal, associate circuit or circuit court that took the plea or imposed the sentence

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then." against Certified docket sheet and judgment from the court of plea or sentence, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record. Order your own criminal record. It supports the agency list and the no-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth? The application cannot be made until at least a year after you turned twenty-one.
What is your current mailing address?
Was the charge a violation of Missouri's minor-in-possession law, § 311.325? If you were charged under a city or county ordinance instead of the state statute, this route may not apply.
Was this the first time you pleaded guilty to or were found guilty of that offense?
Which court sentenced you, and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
On what date were you sentenced, and what was the case number?
Since that conviction, have you been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense, anywhere?

Has your driving licence ever been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it disqualifies you from this expungement.
Are you licensed as a commercial motor vehicle driver, or were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the violation? Either one bars this route.
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the sentencing court, the agency that arrested or cited you, the prosecuting or city attorney and the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division.
Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and your court paperwork and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

customPleadingSpecs.venue: The justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending or in which the arrest record originated. Circuit court for a felony charge dismissed after indictment; justice or municipal court for a citation or lower-court misdemeanour. All 82 counties, 22 circuit court districts, and every municipal and justice court.

rules.filing: File the petition with the proposed order and certificate of service with the clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending. Mississippi has no statewide form; the petition is drafted to the statute and the court, county and prosecuting authority are participant data. Call the clerk before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
rules.fees: No amount is published here. Section 99-19-72 sets a fee for a petition to expunge an offence under § 99-19-71, and subsection (4) sits inside § 99-19-71, but charging a person whose case was dismissed is a contested result and county practice differs. The participant is instructed to confirm the filing fee with the clerk before filing. See the unresolved fee question.
rules.feeWaiver: A pauper's affidavit under general Mississippi practice. Not verified for expungement specifically; the participant asks the clerk.
rules.notice: The prosecuting authority receives a copy. The ten days' written notice to the district attorney is imposed by § 99-19-71(2)(b), which sits inside the felony conviction subsection, and it is NOT imported into this subsection without textual support; the packet nonetheless tells the participant that some districts expect notice and prosecutor approval as a matter of local practice. No response or objection period is stated for this track and no hearing is required by subsection (4).
rules.service: United States mail or hand delivery by the petitioner to the prosecuting authority, contemporaneous with filing, evidenced by the certificate of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank and does not use the archived models' 'by and through his attorney' recital.
rules.notarization: None on the archived models. Whether any district requires verification or notarization is unresolved; the petition carries a simple truth statement rather than a notarized verification.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

A participant who uses this track has not spent their one felony expungement. The one-felony-per-lifetime cap sits in § 99-19-71(2)(a) and applies to conviction expungement, not to subsection (4). That is an important thing to tell people and to encode.
Relief is mandatory. The statute says the court "shall expunge", which is one of very few mandatory record-clearing provisions in the country and should be the headline of the Mississippi product.
The disposition order is obtained by the participant from the clerk and attached as an exhibit. It never delays generation of the petition.

LegalEase pleads the statutory category and does not add the qualifier unless the order itself says so.

Obtaining the district attorney's approval as to form is the practical gate on the entire Mississippi product and it is a negotiation, not a filing. LegalEase prepares the certificate of service, the cover letter and the notice calendar; it does not seek, obtain or negotiate the prosecutor's approval, and a declining or silent prosecutor is an attorney handoff.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the felony?
What felony were you convicted of, and under which Mississippi Code section?
What did your sentence include — incarceration, probation, supervised release, fines, costs, restitution, treatment, or a combination?
On what date did you successfully complete the LAST of all those terms and conditions? Not the conviction date and not your release date.
Are all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence paid in full? This is a separate statutory condition.

Is your conviction any of these: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; first-degree arson; trafficking in controlled substances; a third or subsequent DUI; felon in possession of a firearm; failure to register as a sex offender; voyeurism; witness intimidation; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person; embezzlement; felony procuring prostitution; or promoting prostitution?
Have you ever had a felony conviction expunged in Mississippi before? You are eligible for only one felony expunction in your lifetime.

Were you convicted of more than one felony out of the same set of events? Mississippi counts all convictions arising from a common nucleus of operative facts as ONE conviction and ONE expunction, and the court decides that in its discretion.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the felony?
What felony were you convicted of, and under which Mississippi Code section?
What did your sentence include — incarceration, probation, supervised release, fines, costs, restitution, treatment, or a combination?
On what date did you successfully complete the LAST of all those terms and conditions? Not the conviction date and not your release date.
Are all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence paid in full? This is a separate statutory condition.

Is your conviction any of these: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; first-degree arson; trafficking in controlled substances; a third or subsequent DUI; felon in possession of a firearm; failure to register as a sex offender; voyeurism; witness intimidation; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person; embezzlement; felony procuring prostitution; or promoting prostitution?
Have you ever had a felony conviction expunged in Mississippi before? You are eligible for only one felony expunction in your lifetime.

Were you convicted of more than one felony out of the same set of events? Mississippi counts all convictions arising from a common nucleus of operative facts as ONE conviction and ONE expunction, and the court decides that in its discretion.
Were you a public official, and was the conviction related to your official duties?
In your own words, what have you done since the offence? The court has to decide whether you are rehabilitated, and this is your statement, not ours. A lawyer should review it before you file.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case is under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current address, phone number and email?
Which Mississippi county and city do you live in?

Which court handled the case — justice court, county court, circuit court, or municipal court? Mississippi has four trial court levels that all handle expungements and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case.
Which county was that court in? For a municipal court, which city?
What is the cause or case number?
What were you charged with, and under which Mississippi Code section if you know it?
On what date did the offence happen?
On what date were you arrested or cited?
Which agency arrested or cited you, and what is their case number if you have it?
Which prosecuting authority handled the case — the district attorney for the circuit district, or a county or municipal prosecuting attorney?
On what date were you convicted of the felony?
What felony were you convicted of, and under which Mississippi Code section?
What did your sentence include — incarceration, probation, supervised release, fines, costs, restitution, treatment, or a combination?
On what date did you successfully complete the LAST of all those terms and conditions? Not the conviction date and not your release date.
Are all criminal fines and costs of court imposed in the sentence paid in full? This is a separate statutory condition.

Is your conviction any of these: a crime of violence under § 97-3-2; first-degree arson; trafficking in controlled substances; a third or subsequent DUI; felon in possession of a firearm; failure to register as a sex offender; voyeurism; witness intimidation; abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable person; embezzlement; felony procuring prostitution; or promoting prostitution?
Have you ever had a felony conviction expunged in Mississippi before? You are eligible for only one felony expunction in your lifetime.

Were you convicted of more than one felony out of the same set of events? Mississippi counts all convictions arising from a common nucleus of operative facts as ONE conviction and ONE expunction, and the court decides that in its discretion.
Were you a public official, and was the conviction related to your official duties?
In your own words, what have you done since the offence? The court has to decide whether you are rehabilitated, and this is your statement, not ours. A lawyer should review it before you file.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The order directs every person and agency keeping official records to expunge them EXCEPT fingerprint records, and the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings. Participant-facing copy must not say the record is erased everywhere.

Section 99-19-71(3) expressly provides that the existence of an order of expunction does not preclude an employer from asking a prospective employee whether an order of expunction has been entered on their behalf. This is a real and unusual limitation and participants must be told about it. A person called as a prospective juror must also, on request, advise the court in camera of the previous conviction and expunction.

APPROVE THE CURRENT STATUTORY ROUTES; REPLACE THE PRE-HB 1546 LOGIC. HB 1546 amended Miss. Code § 99-19-71 effective July 1, 2026, so filings after that date must be screened against the amended text.
Ten days' written notice to the district attorney before any hearing, under § 99-19-71(2)(b). This is the one hard timing rule on the track.

rules.notice: Ten (10) days' written notice to the district attorney before any hearing on the petition, under § 99-19-71(2)(b). This is statutory and it is the one hard timing rule on this track. No response or objection period is fixed; the district attorney may appear. A hearing is held as determined in the discretion of the court, and the court may grant if it determines on the record or in writing that the applicant is rehabilitated. A denial must identify the court's findings specifically and not generally.

packetInstructions: Mississippi has no statewide expungement form and § 99-19-71 prescribes none. The four archived petition and order PDFs are Fourth Circuit Court District models covering Leflore, Sunflower and Washington counties only: every county field reads '(Washington, Sunflower, or Leflore)', the certificate of service hardcodes the Fourth District DA at Greenville, the signature blocks are dated 2020, and the orders carry an APPROVED AS TO FORM block. They are drafting references only. Court, county and prosecuting authority are participant-data fields and are never hardcoded.

Build the district-variable fields — court, court level, county, cause number, and the prosecuting authority's name and address — as participant data, never hardcoded. Never default to the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties, or the year 2020.

Tell the participant that Mississippi has no statewide expungement form, that practice varies by county and by circuit district, that some districts expect the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judge will sign, and that they should call the clerk of the court where the case was heard before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.

The one-year waiting period is retained ONLY because § 67-3-70(6) was read from primary authority on this pass — enrolled HB 917 § 34, Laws 2020 ch. 314 — and not because a secondary clearinghouse source reported it. The clock runs from the later of dismissal and discharge or completion of any sentence and payment of any fine.

Relief is mandatory on the statutory findings — 'it shall enter such order' — unlike the discretionary lower-court misdemeanour route. Section 67-3-70 contains no restoration-of-status clause, no perjury-protection clause and no Title 63 carve-out, so participant-facing copy must not import those effects from § 99-19-71.
Instruct the participant to confirm the current waiting period, the correct court and any fee with the clerk before filing.

customPleadingSpecs.venue: A Montana district court in a judicial district where at least one of the convictions occurred (§ 46-18-1105). The underlying convictions will usually have been entered in Justice, Municipal or City Court, but the expungement petition goes to District Court. Where convictions span several districts the participant chooses among them, and the choice has strategic consequences and is never auto-selected.

rules.filing: Unit 1 is a civil petition filed on paper with the clerk of a district court in a judicial district where at least one conviction occurred (§ 46-18-1105). Local district court filing rules apply and the Office of the Court Administrator Court Locator is the published route to local rules and contact information; confirm with the clerk before filing. Unit 2 is a mailed submission to DOJ CRISS after the order issues. Whether any district permits or requires self-represented e-filing for this petition type is unresolved.
rules.fees: $120 for civil commencement of an action by a petitioner, per the Montana Clerks of District Courts civil fee schedule updated May 2024 and issued under §§ 25-1-201, 25-1-202, 3-1-317, 50-15-301 and 25-9-506. The base statutory figure in § 25-1-201(1)(a) is $90; use the published schedule total for the participant-facing number. No fee is charged for the CRISS request. The participant pays for the background check, court document copies and the fingerprinting.
rules.feeWaiver: By statement of inability to pay court costs and fees. The judiciary and Montana Legal Services Association route participants to the MLSA interactive Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees plus a proposed order. That form carries the same non-commercial-use restriction as ER-100 and ER-200, so LegalEase links the participant to the published form and does not reproduce it. Whether a court-approved statewide fee-waiver form exists is unresolved.
rules.notice: § 46-18-1106(1) requires notice to every prosecution office that prosecuted an offence for which expungement is requested. § 46-18-1106(2) gives that office fourteen days from receiving the petition to attempt to notify any victim and to document the attempt. There is no statutory deadline for the prosecution office to respond to the petition itself. § 46-18-1107(1) additionally places on the prosecution office the duty to verify that the petitioner is not detained, charged or subject to pending charges.
rules.service: Mail, hand delivery or email of a file-stamped copy of the petition to each prosecuting office, after filing. Montana files first and then serves; do not reverse it. Victims are notified by the prosecution office, not by the participant.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition under a declaration under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of Montana, giving the city and state where signed, and separately signs the CRISS form. LegalEase leaves both blank.
rules.notarization: none. A declaration under penalty of perjury is used instead.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
LegalEase drafts its own petition, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce ER-100, ER-200, or the MLSA fee-waiver forms.
Do not promise that the court order alone completes expungement. The participant must complete the DOJ CRISS stage under § 46-18-1110(2)(b).

The FD-258 fingerprint step must appear at the front of the participant's task list, not at the end. It is a physical dependency of the CRISS submission and is never a condition of generating the court packet.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.

rules.notice: § 46-18-1106(1) requires notice to every prosecution office that prosecuted an offence for which expungement is requested. § 46-18-1106(2) gives that office fourteen days from receiving the petition to attempt to notify any victim and to document the attempt. packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

The court order is not the end in Montana. Under § 46-18-1110(2)(b) the person whose records are being expunged, not the court and not the clerk, must send the order to the arresting agency, the prosecutor, the clerk and the Department of Justice, together with fingerprints and the DOJ form; § 46-18-204(2) holds the same pattern for deferred dismissals; and the OCA MMRTA instructions say the same. A Montana packet that stops at a signed court order leaves the conviction sitting on the participant's background check.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
LegalEase drafts its own petition, certificate of service, and proposed order. It must not reproduce ER-100, ER-200, or the MLSA fee-waiver forms.
Do not promise that the court order alone completes expungement. The participant must complete the DOJ CRISS stage under § 46-18-1110(2)(b).

The FD-258 fingerprint step must appear at the front of the participant's task list, not at the end. It is a physical dependency of the CRISS submission and is never a condition of generating the court packet.

manualCompletionItems.why: Only where another country's requirements demand it. Left to the participant.

Docket fee $176 under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2). The supreme court may additionally impose a charge not exceeding $19 per case to fund non-judicial personnel; 2026 Senate Bill 430 carries that authority from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030. Some district courts nonetheless accept a poverty affidavit in practice.

In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?

Are you currently required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act?
Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your conviction is not one of them and is not comparable to one of them under a pre-July-2011 offence definition?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?
What documents do you have that show what you have been doing since the case — employment, education, treatment, service, letters of support?

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name?
What was your full name at the time of the arrest, conviction or diversion, if different from your name now?
What sex, race and date of birth should the petition state?
In which Kansas county and which court was the case, and what is the case number?
Which law enforcement agency arrested you?
What offence were you convicted of, and under which Kansas statute?
On what date was the offence committed? This is not the same as the conviction date, and it decides which version of the law applies to you.
On what date were you convicted?
How was the offence classified — a traffic, cigarette or tobacco infraction, a misdemeanour, or a felony? If a felony, what class or grid severity level?
Was the conviction for driving under the influence under K.S.A. 8-1567, and if so was it a first violation or a second or subsequent violation?
On what date did you satisfy the sentence imposed?
On what date were you discharged from probation, a community correctional services programme, parole, postrelease supervision, conditional release or a suspended sentence?
Have you been convicted of a felony in the past two years, or is any felony proceeding pending or being instituted against you?
Are you currently required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act?
Having read the list of offences that cannot be expunged, do you assert that your conviction is not one of them and is not comparable to one of them under a pre-July-2011 offence definition?
In your own words: what has changed in your circumstances and behaviour since the case, and why does expungement matter to you now?
What documents do you have that show what you have been doing since the case — employment, education, treatment, service, letters of support?

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost of obtaining a court order of expungement at five hundred fifty dollars. The clerk collects at the time of filing and Article 983 makes the fees non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Article 983(F) waives all fees where a district attorney certification verifies no felony convictions and no pending felony charge under a bill of information or indictment, together with one of the listed non-conviction grounds — acquittal of all charges after trial including lesser and included offences, no prosecution within the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, dismissal or refusal before the time limitation with no pretrial diversion, factual innocence with entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8, or a juvenile who completed a juvenile drug court programme and is exempt under Article 983(G). The exemption is very often available on this track and must be screened before filing rather than after.

Article 983(F), claimed through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption. The form goes to the district attorney before filing and comes back within fifteen days. Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment. Article 977(A)(2) requires this certification to be included with the motion, and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request that names the exact certification and the five-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it — it is the district attorney's own statement about their records — and its absence is a filing requirement, not a reason to withhold the packet.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 977(A)(2) five-year route. Not required where the conviction was set aside and dismissed under Article 894(B).

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 894(B) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order of dismissal. Where no such order exists and Article 894 relief appears available, obtain it first through the separate Article 987 set-aside track, then return to this one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 977(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 894(B)?" against Certified copy of the Article 894(B) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 977(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Ask the district attorney's office in writing.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the chosen eligibility or fee-exemption basis depends on the absence of pretrial diversion.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional; the track does not depend on it.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 998 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of conviction, at any time after ninety days from the date of conviction. Article 986 makes Article 998 the form to be used for this category; the Article 989 form is not used here.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. The Article 998 motion's prayer asks that where one from each named agency is attached, no contradictory hearing be required and the motion be granted ex parte. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
Race and gender — Article 998 Motion, Part I Defendant Information.
The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 998 Motion, the 'If not represented by counsel' signature block.
Every finding, ruling, date, place and signature on the Article 991 Order — Article 991 Order — the ordering paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.

Every granting or denying paragraph, finding, date, place and signature on the Article 992 Order of Expungement — Article 992 Order of Expungement — the decretal paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

The ordinary Article 983(A) cap of five hundred fifty dollars now applies. The three-hundred-dollar cap formerly in Article 983(M) — fifty dollars each to the Bureau, the sheriff and the district attorney and one hundred fifty to the clerk — was null, void and without effect and terminated on 1 August 2026 under Article 983(M)(5), and is now historical only. The clerk collects at filing and the fees are non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
Article 983(F) through the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, whose grounds are non-conviction grounds and therefore rarely reach a conviction track.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge. Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?" against Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the first offender pardon. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F). Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.

Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.
