generationRequirements.question: Is any criminal charge pending against you now?
Had you ever been convicted of a felony before this one?
Have all court costs for this conviction been paid?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked on the first offender pardon route. No pardon issues while court costs remain unpaid, and this is the common, fixable failure point.

generationRequirements.question: Is the offence a crime of violence under R.S. 14:2(B)?

Is the offence one of these six — aggravated battery, second degree battery, aggravated criminal damage to property, simple robbery, purse snatching, or illegal use of weapons or dangerous instrumentalities?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the offence is or may be a crime of violence, because Article 978(E) is the only lane that reaches those six.

generationRequirements.question: Is the offence a sex offence, or a criminal offence against a victim who is a minor, as defined by R.S. 15:541?
Is the offence a violation of the Uniform Controlled Dangerous Substances Law?

If it is a drug offence, which of these fits — simple possession under R.S. 40:966(C), 967(C), 968(C), 969(C) or 970(C); possession with intent to distribute; an offence punishable by not more than five years; an offence eligible under Article 893(E); or an offence for which you are entitled to a first offender pardon?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked only where the offence is a controlled dangerous substance violation, because Article 978(B)(3) bars the class and then names five exceptions.

generationRequirements.question: Was the conviction for domestic abuse battery?
Was this conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated?
Does the record of this arrest name anyone besides you?
Are you now in the physical custody of the Department of Public Safety and Corrections serving a sentence at hard labour?

manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page

manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Recorded by counsel as a limitation; place when the packet is drafted.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge. Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution. Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Has a court already signed an order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution under Article 893(E)?" against Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution, and correct the packet if they disagree.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the first offender pardon. Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Minute entry showing the final disposition. Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984. Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F). Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency. The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

participantActionRequired.description: Every finding, ruling, date, place and signature on the Article 991 Order — Article 991 Order — the ordering paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.

Every granting or denying paragraph, finding, date, place and signature on the Article 992 Order of Expungement — Article 992 Order of Expungement — the decretal paragraphs, the date and place line and the judge's signature line.
Race and gender — Article 989 Motion, Part I Defendant Information.
The participant's signature and the date of signing — Article 989 Motion, unrepresented-mover signature block on the final page.
Every certification box and the district attorney's signature on the Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption — Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, the certification section and signature block.
The whole of the Article 990 Affidavit of Response — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The clerk's service of the motion and of the order and judgment — Not printed in the participant packet; described in the filing instructions only.
The mover signs the Article 989 Motion in the block headed 'If not represented by counsel'. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

Article 983(A) caps the total cost at five hundred fifty dollars, collected by the clerk at filing and non-refundable even if the motion is denied. Where the conviction is for operating a vehicle while intoxicated, Article 984(C) assesses a further fifty-dollar court cost payable to the Office of Motor Vehicles. On the first offender pardon route the participant must also have paid the underlying court costs of the conviction, which is a precondition of the pardon rather than an expungement fee.

Article 983(F) through the Article 988 form in principle, but Louisiana State Police states that a person is ineligible for the exemption if they have ever been convicted of a felony, including an expunged felony. On a felony conviction track the exemption will almost never be available, and the packet says so rather than implying a waiver that will be refused.
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only when the participant cannot pay the filing fee.

participantActionRequired.description: The participant does not serve anyone. Under Article 979 the clerk of court serves notice of the motion by United States mail or electronically on the district attorney of the parish of conviction, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency, and files a certificate of service showing the mailing date. Under Article 982, if expungement is granted the clerk serves the order and judgment on the district attorney, the Bureau, the sheriff of the parish of conviction and the arresting agency.

File the Article 989 Motion for Expungement with the proposed Article 991 Order and the proposed Article 992 Order of Expungement with the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction. Article 972.1 gives district courts, city and parish courts, mayor's and traffic courts, juvenile and family courts, and the New Orleans municipal and traffic courts authority within their trial jurisdiction. Article 986 provides that only the forms in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995 and 998 shall be used, so there is no drafted pleading and no local variant; Article 986(C) lets a clerk alter the form only to show the name of that court.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days. The Article 994 form requires it on its face. Louisiana State Police recommends the fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, ORIGINAL arrest charge, arrest number and counts — and on this track the original felony arrest charge is the thing being expunged. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What felony charge or charges were you arrested for originally? Give the statute and offence name for each, taken from the arrest record rather than from the charge you were finally convicted of." against Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Bill of information or indictment for each charge. Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.

participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney. The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantActionRequired.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 — the assertion of no other adult criminal convictions in Maine
manualCompletionItems.why: Paragraph 3 of CR-218 Rev. 7/24 reads in full: 'Defendant has no other adult criminal convictions in Maine and has not had a case dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition since completing their sentence for this offense.' The trailing time limit governs the deferred-disposition clause but not the convictions clause, so the form asks the participant to swear to an unbounded absence of Maine convictions while § 2262(3) bars only a conviction SINCE the person fully satisfied the sentence for their most recent eligible criminal conviction. A participant with an old prior that predates the completion date is not disqualified by the statute but reads as disqualified on the form. LegalEase does not answer this paragraph either way: it prints it blank, sets out both readings in plain terms, and tells the participant to complete it themselves and to take advice before filing if they have an older prior.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 1's assertion that the crime is eligible for sealing under 15 M.R.S. § 2261(6)
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether a crime is a current or former Class E crime, and whether a pre-2017 marijuana offence matches one of the five listed subparagraphs, is a legal conclusion requiring the judgment and the historical statute. The participant owns it.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraphs 5 and 7, paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection, the participant's signature and date, the case number, the hearing details, and the judge's findings and signature on CR370 are all left blank by design.

none. CR360 uses a declaration under penalty of perjury rather than a notarial acknowledgment. This is the opposite of CR145 on the § 610.122 track, which must be subscribed and sworn before a notary, judge or clerk, and the two must not be conflated in participant copy.

Standard circuit court filing fees and costs apply, and they vary by county. Rule 155.02 governs filing fees and costs for an expungement action. The former $250 expungement surcharge under § 488.650 was repealed effective 28 August 2023 and must never be quoted. A petition filed with the clerk of the Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.2(1)). generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What was the offense? Was it a drink- or drug-driving offense, or a boating offense?
Was it charged as a state misdemeanor, or as a county or city ordinance violation? A felony is not eligible under this section.
On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then.
Which court took your plea or sentenced you — the municipal division, the associate circuit division, or the circuit court — and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
What was the case number?
Was this your first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, anywhere? The section reaches a first offense only.
Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?

Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly.
Do you have any drink- or drug-driving charge, boating offense, or licence suspension or revocation proceeding pending right now?

Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense.
Were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offense?
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever, and it cannot be undone.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the court, the arresting agency, the prosecuting or city attorney, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
Have you checked your driver record and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

Participant-facing copy says sealed, never destroyed.

packetInstructions: Automatic record relief is not a dismissal, sealing or expungement. The record stays on the state summary criminal history and a notation is added, which controls whether the record is disseminated to employers and agencies conducting fingerprint background checks under PC 11105(k) through (p).
The absence of a notation does not mean ineligibility. The DOJ evaluates millions of records monthly back to 1973 and says no additional action is needed to receive relief.

Commercial background check companies do not access DOJ records at all and may hold stale data. Law enforcement, the Commission on Teacher Credentialing, school districts and their contractors continue to see conviction history.

packetInstructions: The offense class and the maximum sentence that could have been imposed are determined based on the law in effect at the time the offense was committed, not current law. § 54-142a(e)(1)(B).

If a case has more than one count and any count is not erasable, nothing on that record is erased. The same rule appears at § 54-142a(i)(1), § 54-142u(b) and § 54-142v(b). This is the most common practical defeat in Connecticut.

DUI is not excluded from Clean Slate. § 14-227a is carved out of the seven-year misdemeanor bucket and placed in the ten-year bucket. The only DUI bar is a second § 14-227a conviction within the ten years following.
Firearms offenses are not a category exclusion. § 54-142a(e)(2)(C) is an enumerated list of statute sections and must be screened section by section, not by category label.

Erasure does not terminate the obligation to pay an unremitted fine imposed as part of the sentence, and it does not end sex offender, deadly weapon offender or felony-for-a-sexual-purpose registration obligations, or a standing criminal protective order. Nothing in the erasure provisions requires the DMV to erase criminal history information on a driving record, which matters to any CDL holder.

packetInstructions: Consumer-facing copy must say "restrict" and, separately, "seal." Georgia does not use "expungement" in the statute and has not since July 1, 2013, and neither remedy destroys the record.

The packet must state that a restriction or sealing may still be used to disqualify the participant from employment or office in the same manner as a first offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, and does not supersede disclosure required by federal law. The packet must never tell a participant they may state the record does not exist.

The filing is made in the existing criminal case under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant, in the court that handled the case. It is not a new civil action, is not captioned IN RE, and does not carry a Civil Action No.

The proposed order must name the OTN and arrest date, name GCIC and the county agencies by category, name the clerk and court, and limit disclosure to what § 35-3-37(t) and (v) permit. A restriction order that does not name GCIC is not actionable.

Every packet carries a plain-language instruction to confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing. No statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

Where a hearing is requested it must be held within 90 days of filing, and the motion asks in the alternative that the matter be set for hearing within 90 days. There is no prosecutor objection window on this route; the 90 days is a deadline for holding a hearing, not a period for the prosecuting attorney to object.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Confidentiality by operation of law — classification and verification, no filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The base branch. Where the disposition falls inside the 16 M.R.S. § 703(2) list the record is already confidential criminal history record information and there is nothing to file: no court has any role, no motion exists, and generating CR-218 for a non-conviction would be affirmatively wrong because § 2262 reaches a specific criminal conviction only. The unit classifies the disposition against the § 703(2) list, explains that the confidentiality is automatic, walks the participant through obtaining their own State Bureau of Identification record to see what the State actually holds, and states plainly where the disposition falls outside the list that Maine offers no relief for it rather than routing them to a motion that will be denied. It also separates the three problems that participants conflate: the Bureau record, the court docket, and a private vendor's database.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Court-ordered and automatic Article XIV relief — verification, no participant filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The first branch, and it is a legally distinct mechanism rather than a preliminary check. Article XIV, section 2 directs the courts themselves to order expungement for people who have completed their sentences, on constitutional deadlines the courts were given, and automatically vacates the sentence and terminates supervision for a person on probation or parole without any petition at all. For both of those populations there is no participant filing, no application, no request and no form: the constitution puts the act on the court. CR375 confirms the design from the other direction — its two selectable postures are currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation, so a participant presently on probation or parole for a marijuana offense fits neither box, because the constitution does not ask them to petition. The unit's output is therefore verification and explanation: identify the marijuana case and the sentencing county, check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record to see whether expungement was already ordered, and, where it was, help the participant ask the court for the certificate of expungement the constitution requires it to issue. Where relief was not entered the participant is routed to the second unit. What the unit must not do is promise that relief occurred: the constitution directed the courts to process these cases, and a direction is not a receipt.

generationRequirements.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

generationRequirements.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

packetInstructions: Automatic relief runs first. Where the charge was dismissed on identity grounds the packet checks whether the § 610.145.1(2) order was already entered before offering a petition, because a participant who files for relief the court was already obliged to enter pays for nothing.

The costs of expunging the records are not taxed against the person eligible for expungement (§ 610.145.3), and any licence or privilege reinstatement fee is waived (§ 610.145.5). The packet tells the participant so, and tells them to raise it with the clerk if a fee is demanded.

The ancillary relief in §§ 610.145.4 to 6 is set out in full, because it is unusually broad and participants do not know to ask for it: Department of Revenue expungement, reversal of administrative actions including licence points, suspensions and revocations, a certified corrected driver history at no cost, licence reinstatement at no cost, Department of Corrections and other-agency expungement and reversal, and an insurer's obligation to refund three years of additional premium charged on insurance points from the matter.
Venue is the court where the charge was last pending, which on a case that moved is not the court it started in. The packet says so and directs the participant to the docket.
The certified docket, the proof of the identity problem and the driver record are obtained by the participant before filing. LegalEase never holds or assesses any of them, and none delays generation.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Automatic expungement on prosecutor or judicial-officer notice — no participant filing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The first branch, and the statute itself calls it automatic. Under § 610.145.1(2), where the participant was named in a charge because another person used their identifying information or because of mistaken identity and that charge is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall notify the court and the court shall order the expungement. There is no petition, no motion, no application and no form: the duty is on the prosecutor or the judicial officer, and § 610.145.3 confirms it by describing the beneficiary as the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. That has a direct product consequence, which is why this is a unit rather than a footnote: generating CR301 for a participant whose charge was dismissed on exactly this ground asks a court for relief the law has already told it to enter, and may cost them a filing fee for nothing. The unit's output is verification and explanation — check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record, ask the clerk whether an expungement order was entered on the dismissal, and understand that the participant may still identify agencies for the order to reach, because § 610.145.3 extends that right to the automatic beneficiary as well as to a petitioner. Where the order was not entered, the participant moves to the second unit.

destination.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol central repository, with the Office of the State Courts Administrator
destination.detail: The central repository screens the statewide criminal history database on a rolling basis not less than once per week, expunges eligible offenses, reflects the change through the Missouri uniform law enforcement system, and notifies both the Supreme Court of Missouri and the Office of the State Courts Administrator; the Office of the State Courts Administrator then expunges the corresponding case records in the statewide court automation system. The participant submits nothing to either body. Where an eligible offense is not expunged, § 610.141.8 makes the filing of a § 610.140 petition the sole remedy, which is the mo-610-140-conviction track.

rules.filing: none. § 610.141 creates no petition, application, request or submission of any kind for the participant. The central repository screens and expunges of its own motion and the Office of the State Courts Administrator expunges the corresponding case records on the repository's designations. Where an eligible offense is not expunged, § 610.141.8 makes the filing of a § 610.140 petition the sole remedy.
rules.fees: none. The mechanism costs the participant nothing because nothing is filed. § 610.144 creates the Missouri Expungement Fund to pay for the technology from appropriations, gifts, donations, grants and bequests. The participant pays only for any record they choose to obtain to check the outcome.
rules.feeWaiver: none. There is no fee to waive.
rules.notice: none to the participant. The central repository notifies the Supreme Court of Missouri weekly of expunged offense changes and notifies the Office of the State Courts Administrator of its eligibility designations. § 610.141.12 directs the Office of the State Courts Administrator, the Department of Corrections and the Patrol jointly to develop an explanatory document to be given by a sentencing court at sentencing and by a probation or parole officer on release from supervision, which is the only participant-facing communication the section provides for and which is prospective rather than a notice that an expungement has occurred.
rules.service: none. Nothing is served.
rules.participantSignature: none. The participant signs nothing on this track.

generationRequirements.question: Is the conviction for possessing a controlled substance, or for drug paraphernalia? Missouri's automatic expungement law reaches only those four offenses — it does not reach trafficking, distribution, delivery or manufacture.
Was it a misdemeanor or a felony? And if a felony, was it a class A felony? A class A felony is excluded.
On what date did you finish everything the court ordered and were released from any custody or supervision? The law calls that final disposition, and the one-year or three-year clock runs from it.
Was this the only conviction in that case? If the same case included a conviction for something that is not one of the four covered offenses, the automatic law does not reach any of it.
Since that date, have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any outstanding arrest, warrant or pending criminal charge right now?

Have you had any Missouri expungement before, under any law? From the date the automatic law starts operating, automatic expungements and petition expungements share the same lifetime limits — three misdemeanors and two felonies between them.

Do you need this record cleared by a particular date — for a job, a licence, housing or an immigration matter? The automatic mechanism has no published start date beyond a 1 January 2027 outer limit and cannot be relied on for a deadline.

Knowing that a petition under § 610.140 is available now but costs a filing fee and uses one of your lifetime slots, and that automatic relief is free but not yet shown to be running and uses the same slot, would you like to talk through which makes sense for you?

packetInstructions: The scope is four offenses, not a category. § 610.141 reaches possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, and unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074. Trafficking, distribution, delivery and manufacture are outside it, and Missouri must never be described as a general clean-slate state.

Automatic expungement consumes a lifetime slot. § 610.141.6 limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under §§ 610.140 and 610.141 combined, counting only the highest-level offense where a case contains more than one. This closes the review's cap-coordination build blocker and belongs on the § 610.140 packet as well as this one.

The relief is closure of the record under § 610.120, which § 610.141.1(4) says in terms. It is the same legal effect as a § 610.140 order, not destruction, and the packet must not describe it as erasure.

The participant must be told the uncertainty and the alternative together. The section operates when technically feasible and no later than 1 January 2027, no implementation notice has been published, and a § 610.140 petition is available now. Telling a participant to wait for future relief without explaining both is not acceptable.

The sole remedy for a failure to expunge is a § 610.140 petition, which § 610.141.8 provides notwithstanding any other provision of law. There is no appeal to the Highway Patrol and no correction application, and the guidance routes a participant whose record was missed to the petition track rather than to an agency.

Secondary summaries of Missouri clean slate must not be used. The enacted § 610.141 is narrower than the press coverage and differs materially from SB 1494, the broader vehicle that did not become law but whose text is widely conflated with it — including a bulk-processing deadline that appears nowhere in the enacted section. Only the enrolled CCS SS SB 1421 text governs.

destination.name: Clerk of the court in which the case was pending
destination.detail: Paper filing with the clerk of the originating court, with the proposed order tendered alongside. The prosecuting authority is served with a copy.

rules.filing: File the petition with the proposed order and certificate of service with the clerk of the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the case was pending. Mississippi has no statewide form; the petition is drafted to the statute and the court, county and prosecuting authority are participant data. Call the clerk before filing to ask whether that court has its own preferred form or additional requirements.
rules.fees: No amount is published here. Section 99-19-72 sets a fee for a petition to expunge an offence under § 99-19-71, and subsection (4) sits inside § 99-19-71, but charging a person whose case was dismissed is a contested result and county practice differs. The participant is instructed to confirm the filing fee with the clerk before filing. See the unresolved fee question.
rules.feeWaiver: A pauper's affidavit under general Mississippi practice. Not verified for expungement specifically; the participant asks the clerk.
rules.notice: The prosecuting authority receives a copy. The ten days' written notice to the district attorney is imposed by § 99-19-71(2)(b), which sits inside the felony conviction subsection, and it is NOT imported into this subsection without textual support; the packet nonetheless tells the participant that some districts expect notice and prosecutor approval as a matter of local practice. No response or objection period is stated for this track and no hearing is required by subsection (4).
rules.service: United States mail or hand delivery by the petitioner to the prosecuting authority, contemporaneous with filing, evidenced by the certificate of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank and does not use the archived models' 'by and through his attorney' recital.
rules.notarization: None on the archived models. Whether any district requires verification or notarization is unresolved; the petition carries a simple truth statement rather than a notarized verification.

processGuidanceSpecs.unitLabel: Intervention court — verification of the self-executing result, and routing
processGuidanceSpecs.unitDescription: The verification branch. Section 9-23-23 states a result rather than a procedure: on completion of all requirements the charge and prosecution 'shall be dismissed', and where the person was sentenced at the time of the guilty plea completion 'will result in the record of the criminal conviction or adjudication being expunged'. There is no petition language, no application, no fee, no hearing, no notice and no waiting period anywhere in the section — which is unique in the Mississippi scheme and is why no petition is generated on this branch. The section does not, however, direct any officer to enter or transmit an order, so whether an expungement order in fact issues without the participant asking is a matter of local practice and is preserved as an open question. The correct product output is therefore verification: establish from the clerk what was actually entered and when, obtain a certified copy of any dismissal or expungement order that already exists, and route onward only where the record shows relief did not issue. Implied consent violations are expressly barred from expunction here and route to the DUI track.

packetInstructions: Montana's three words are not interchangeable and participant copy must keep them apart. Expungement under § 46-18-1103(1) means to permanently destroy, delete or erase a record from the criminal history record information system maintained by the Department of Justice. What happens at the courts, law-enforcement agencies and prosecutors' offices is sealing, not destruction (§ 46-18-1110(2)(a)). Removal is the DOJ term for deleting a non-conviction record. Redesignation and resentencing are MMRTA outcomes and are neither.

A DOJ removal or expungement does not reach public county court records. Montana has no centralised court records system, so each county court must be searched separately, and a participant who successfully clears the DOJ record may still find the case on a county court portal. Participant-facing copy must say so.

The two-portal court search is a required participant step, not a suggestion: one search of the Montana Public Access Portal for District Courts and one for Courts of Limited Jurisdiction. Montana has no centralised court records system, and some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check at all.
DOJ states that after July 1, 2017 CRISS will automatically remove all non-conviction arrest data per MCA 44-5-202 and no Record Removal Form is required. Do not generate a form for this route.

Where the record persists, contact the court of jurisdiction and ask it to send the final outcome to the Montana Department of Justice, then fall back to the non-conviction removal request route. The fallback request is not evidence that the automatic mechanism itself has a filing.
CHOPRS requests may experience a hold of up to 72 hours, and both Montana Public Access Portals must be searched separately.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Strongly encouraged by the form where applicable.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Deliver a copy of the application to the prosecutor. The delivery method the court expects is not yet confirmed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: California DOJ state summary criminal history
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: California Department of Justice
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional. CR-180 expressly says a RAP sheet is not required.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own record through the DOJ 'Criminal Records, Request Your Own' process. It is fingerprint-based through Live Scan and a fee waiver process exists. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is unsure which statute box applies.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of conviction for the docket and disposition. It fixes the statute box.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Local cover or electronic consent form
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The Superior Court of the filing county
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the county publishes one. San Luis Obispo requires form ECS-1 electronic consent or a self-addressed stamped envelope.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the county self-help centre which local forms accompany a CR-180 petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is unsure whether probation was granted.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of conviction. The docket is what settles the probation question and therefore the statute box.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket and disposition, including the sentence and any supervision term
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant cannot state the sentence type or completion date from memory.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of conviction for the docket. It settles which of the three sub-routes applies.

participantFilingRequirements.name: California DOJ state summary criminal history
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: California Department of Justice
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional supporting record.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own record through the DOJ 'Criminal Records, Request Your Own' process. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket, abstract of judgment and disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of conviction. The record is what the participant uses to confirm the realignment question, which LegalEase does not decide.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court records showing the case resolution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: One of the two evidence routes on the form. The alternative is the petitioner's declaration under penalty of perjury.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court for the docket showing the DEJ completion and dismissal. Where records are unavailable, the form permits a declaration under penalty of perjury instead.

participantFilingRequirements.name: California DOJ state summary criminal history

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing the offense code section as charged and convicted
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Superior Court of the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of conviction. The exact code section is what determines whether the offense is a wobbler or is listed in PC 19.8(a).

participantFilingRequirements.name: Arrest report or arresting agency record showing the report number
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting law enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the arresting agency for the report number and arrest record. The petition requires the arresting agency and report number, which most participants will not have to hand. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket showing the disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court where the accusatory pleading was filed

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court where the pleading was filed for the docket showing how the charges ended.

participantFilingRequirements.name: California DOJ state summary criminal history

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional. Useful where the participant cannot identify the arrest details.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own record through the DOJ 'Criminal Records, Request Your Own' process. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up to confirm the docket number, the conviction date and the full count list.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up to confirm the docket number, the conviction date and the statute of conviction. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect it.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Connecticut Board of Pardons and Paroles

participantFilingRequirements.name: Judicial Branch case look-up printout
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Connecticut Judicial Branch online case look-up
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up to confirm the docket number and conviction details. An erased case will not appear.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that sealed the record for a certified copy of the order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of Eligibility
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Florida Department of Law Enforcement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Apply again to FDLE at the ten-year point. Do not file the court packet until the valid certificate is obtained.

participantFilingRequirements.name: FDLE personal review criminal history
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Florida Department of Law Enforcement
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: To verify whether automatic sealing actually happened.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request an FDLE personal review; FDLE charges no fee for a personal review.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Agency-head or prosecutor certification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The head of the arresting agency, or the State Attorney
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the head of the arresting agency, or the State Attorney, to complete the certification section of the application. LegalEase does not obtain or review it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Prosecutor certification that the dismissal was because of lawful self-defense
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The State Attorney for the circuit
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the State Attorney's office to complete the certification. It is obtained by persuasion rather than by form; LegalEase does not obtain or review it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Documentation supporting victim status
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records, service providers, or law enforcement
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: As the statute and the court require.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The participant gathers what they have and what a service provider can supply. LegalEase does not collect or assess it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certification of successful diversion completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The State Attorney or the diversion program
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the State Attorney's office or the diversion program to complete the certification.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of program completion
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The diversion program
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request written proof of completion from the program.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Fingerprints
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A law enforcement agency or authorised fingerprint vendor
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Have fingerprints taken and submit them with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified statement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The State Attorney
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the certified statement from the State Attorney's office.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified dispositions
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for certified copies of the dispositions.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Fingerprints
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A law enforcement agency or authorised fingerprint vendor
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Have fingerprints taken and submit them with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments and that requirements vary by agency. Bring government photo identification and the agency's fee. The GCIC lobby office is by appointment only. Read the report for whether each charge shows a final disposition and whether the cycle is already marked restricted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the disposition is missing from or wrong on the Georgia criminal history.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for a certified copy of the final disposition. Where the court has not transmitted the disposition to GCIC at all, the correction process at § 35-3-37(d) through (g) is the unblocking step.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report and confirm the arrest appears. If the arrest appears on neither the Georgia nor the FBI criminal history, the restriction cannot be processed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official documentation of the disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where the disposition does not appear on the Georgia criminal history.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for official documentation of the final disposition and attach it to the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Money order or certified check for the GCIC record restriction processing fee, payable to "Georgia Bureau of Investigation"
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's bank or a money-order issuer
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required at the point an approved application goes to GCIC, and not required where the prosecuting attorney approves and enters the restriction directly in the CCH interface.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The GCIC record restriction processing fee is $25.00 on the GCIC fee schedule effective 1 January 2025 and in the form instructions. Applications missing the fee are returned unprocessed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report and check whether the arrest cycle is already marked restricted. This is a diagnostic step, not a filing requirement.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting or accusing court for a copy of the final disposition and attach it to the filing as the referenced exhibit.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of sentence completion, such as a probation termination order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court, or the supervising probation office
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court or the supervising probation office for the order terminating probation or documentation that the sentence was completed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report showing the case is restricted
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report and confirm the cycle shows as restricted. It is effectively required on this route because it is the proof of the first statutory element. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a copy of the final disposition and enclose it with the motion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pardon certificate
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: State Board of Pardons and Paroles
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a copy of the pardon certificate from the State Board of Pardons and Paroles and attach it to the petition. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting or accusing court for a copy of the final disposition and attach it to the filing as the referenced exhibit.
