participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting or accusing court for a copy of the final disposition and attach it to the filing as the referenced exhibit.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the dead docket entry or the case docket showing the dead docket date
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the charge is pending
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court where the charge is pending for the docket showing when the charge was placed on the dead docket. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The order vacating or reversing the conviction, and proof the decision became final
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court, or the clerk of the appellate or post-conviction court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that vacated or reversed the conviction for a copy of the order, and the clerk of the convicting court for the docket entries showing the appellate process is complete. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report showing the fugitive warrant arrest cycle
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report and identify the arrest cycle for the fugitive warrant. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Any Georgia court record of the fugitive warrant proceeding
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the fugitive warrant matter was heard
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where a Georgia court record of the matter exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket or disposition of the fugitive warrant proceeding.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the offence is already restricted — your Georgia criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or the court order restricting the record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC; or the clerk of the court that entered the order
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own criminal history report showing the cycle as restricted, or a copy of the restricting order from the clerk, and enclose it with the request. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: To confirm afterwards that the restriction was entered.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the report after sentencing and confirm the first offender cycle is restricted. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Final disposition showing the First Offender sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced you
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the final disposition showing that you were sentenced under the First Offender Act, and attach it to the petition as Exhibit A. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Final disposition showing the First Offender sentence, and the discharge order where one was entered
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced you and granted the discharge
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the final disposition showing that you were sentenced under the First Offender Act, and for the discharge order if one was entered, and attach them to the petition as Exhibit A. A discharge frequently was never entered; where that is so, the petition says you were discharged as a matter of law. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates these records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The sentencing record and plea paperwork from the original case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for the sentencing record, the plea transcript or plea paperwork, and the final disposition. These are what an attorney or legal-aid desk will need to assess the eligibility claim and approach the prosecuting attorney.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own Georgia criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Most Georgia sheriff's offices and police departments, or GCIC
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant relies on it or the court expects it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: GBI's guidance says a Georgia criminal history record can be obtained from most sheriff's offices or police departments, with requirements varying by agency. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Include a copy of your photo identification with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Money order for the application fee
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A post office, bank or store that issues money orders
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a money order for the HCJDC fee and enclose it with the application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope so HCJDC can return the result.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition showing discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the discharge and dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification, money order, and stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents, a money order issuer, and a post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose a copy of your photo identification, a money order for the fee, and a stamped self-addressed envelope.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition showing discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the discharge and dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application. LegalEase does not review the court order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Photo identification, money order, and stamped self-addressed envelope
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own documents, a money order issuer, and a post office
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Enclose these with the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application. LegalEase does not review the court order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order granting expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The sentencing court, at stage 1
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the signed order from the sentencing court and attach it to the HCJDC application.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk that all financial obligations in this case are paid
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in this case number. Rule 2.83(3) counts only obligations in the case or cases where expungement is sought, and room and board fees sought under a separate civil action under § 356.7 are not counted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check, dated within the past 30 days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Submit form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature through the state portal. The Iowa Judicial Branch instructions state a request costs $15. The check must be dated within 30 days of filing, so obtain it and then file promptly.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk that all financial obligations in this case are paid
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in this case number. Rule 2.83(3) counts only obligations in the case where expungement is sought.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk of the balance in the case containing the deferred judgment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the Iowa District Court for the county of the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the balance in that case number. An unpaid balance is the usual reason an expected automatic expungement did not happen.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official DCI Iowa criminal history record check on form DCI-77, dated within the past 30 days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Iowa Department of Public Safety, Division of Criminal Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Submit form DCI-77 with a release authorization signature through the state portal. The Iowa Judicial Branch instructions state a request costs $15. Obtain it and then file the § 901C.3 application promptly, because it expires after 30 days.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified court order of acquittal stating not guilty of the charged crimes, or certified court order of dismissal showing which crimes were dismissed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that heard the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that heard the case for a certified copy of the order of acquittal or dismissal.

participantFilingRequirements.name: One charging document: criminal citation, or criminal complaint and summons showing service by the sheriff's office, or an indictment, or an information
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that heard the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a copy from the court that heard the case.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Idaho State Police, Bureau of Criminal Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Not required as an attachment, but needed to build the petition accurately.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a criminal history report from the Idaho State Police Bureau of Criminal Identification.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case information from the iCourt Portal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: iCourt Portal at mycourts.idaho.gov, or the court where the case was filed
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant does not already know the case number, charges, statute sections, level, supervision end date, or completion date.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look the case up on the iCourt Portal at mycourts.idaho.gov, or ask the court where the case was filed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Illinois State Police statewide criminal history transcript
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Illinois State Police, Bureau of Identification, through the Access and Review process
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Attend an Illinois law enforcement or correctional facility or a licensed fingerprint vendor, submit fingerprints and identifying information, and receive the transcript. Access and Review is free on the ISP fee schedule.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Chicago Police Department RAP sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Chicago Police Department
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where there were Chicago arrests; the statewide transcript does not always capture them.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the RAP sheet from the Chicago Police Department. A local fee applies.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified disposition for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit clerk of each county where a case was filed
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask each circuit clerk's office for a certified copy of the disposition, and confirm copy counts, filing method and the exact fee while you are there.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Attend an Illinois law enforcement or correctional facility or a licensed fingerprint vendor, submit fingerprints and identifying information, and receive the transcript. Access and Review is free on the ISP fee schedule.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask each circuit clerk for a certified copy of the disposition, and confirm copy counts, filing method and the exact fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The Governor's pardon specifically authorizing expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Illinois Prisoner Review Board or the Office of the Governor
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of the executed pardon. The petition depends on the pardon expressly authorizing expungement.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: School, college or awarding body
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of your high school diploma, GED, college diploma or transcripts.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Employment documentation for the last five years
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Employers or tax records
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Provide W-2s, tax returns, paycheck stubs or a letter from your employers covering the last five years.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of completion of any counselling
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Counselling provider
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant attended anger management, marriage, substance-abuse or similar counselling.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the provider for proof of completion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: DD-214 or similar proof of military service
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: National Personnel Records Center or the service branch
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant served in the military, and required for the military certificate branch.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a copy of your DD-214.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Fingerprint-based criminal history
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: As directed in Guidelines paragraph B-5
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Follow paragraph B-5 of the Board's Guidelines for when and how to obtain fingerprints for criminal history.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that granted the original expungement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that granted the expungement for a certified copy of the order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the original expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that granted the expungement
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the granting court for a certified copy of the order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the clerk of whether a non-disclosure order was entered
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the infraction was handled
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk whether the court entered an order under I.C. 34-28-5-15 in the cause.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own case information from the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting district court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the convicting court for the case number, the offence of conviction and the date the sentence was satisfied or supervision discharged. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates these records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own evidence of the intervening years, for the (h)(2) and (h)(3) findings
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own employment, education, treatment, service and community records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended for the discretionary findings at the hearing; the packet generates without it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Assemble your own records and letters. LegalEase formats what you supply and assesses none of it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Pay the clerk when you file. The supreme court may impose an additional charge not exceeding $19 per case. Confirm the current total with the clerk.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own diversion agreement and the record showing its terms were fulfilled
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court, or the diverting prosecuting authority
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the diverting authority for the diversion agreement and the record of successful completion. The fulfilment date is what starts your waiting period. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates these records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own evidence of the intervening years, for the (h)(2) and (h)(3) findings
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own employment, education, treatment, service and community records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended for the discretionary findings at the hearing; the packet generates without it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Assemble your own records and letters. LegalEase formats what you supply and assesses none of it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Pay the clerk when you file. Confirm the current total with the clerk.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own case information from the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting district court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the case number, the disposition and the date the sentence or diversion terms were completed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Any material you choose to bring in support of the coercion element
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records, or an advocate assisting them
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Entirely the participant's choice; the packet generates without it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Bring whatever you have. LegalEase does not collect, inspect, authenticate or assess it and does not decide whether it proves coercion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Pay the clerk when you file.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that you completed the specialty court programme
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The specialty court programme coordinator or the district court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask your programme coordinator or the court for the certificate or order recording completion of the programme requirements. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge, unless the court waives all or part of it
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Unless and to the extent the court grants the K.S.A. 21-6614(a)(3) waiver.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk how the court handles a fee-waiver request on a specialty court petition, and pay whatever is not waived.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Any court record showing the disposition of the charges
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court where the charges were filed
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where charges were filed and dismissed, or where a court found no probable cause, or where the participant was found not guilty.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket or the order of dismissal, acquittal or finding of no probable cause.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee of $176, plus any non-judicial personnel charge, unless a statutory fee exemption applies
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Not payable where K.S.A. 22-2410(b)(3)(B) applies, which is broader than identity theft alone.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk whether the statutory fee exemption applies to you before paying.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own municipal case information
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The municipal court clerk
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the municipal court clerk for the case number, the ordinance violated, the disposition, the completion date, and whether all costs and fines are paid. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates these records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The municipal court's own expungement form, where it publishes one
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The municipal court clerk or the city's website
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the municipal court publishes its own instrument, which governs over the statewide fallback.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk whether the court has its own form. Wichita and Topeka both publish their own.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The municipal filing fee, where the court charges one
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the municipal court clerk
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: K.S.A. 12-4516(g)(2) lets a municipal court prescribe a fee as costs; amounts vary by court.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk what that court charges.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Any municipal court record showing the disposition of the ordinance charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The municipal court clerk
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and dismissed, or the participant was found not guilty, or a court found no probable cause.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the municipal court clerk for the docket or the order. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The municipal court's own expungement form, where it publishes one
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The municipal court clerk or the city's website
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the municipal court publishes its own instrument, which governs over the statewide fallback.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk whether the court has its own form.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The municipal filing fee, where the court charges one and no exemption applies
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the municipal court clerk
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: No fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk what that court charges and tell them if you were arrested as a result of identity theft.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own registration history
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The local law enforcement agency that registers you, or the Kansas Bureau of Investigation
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the agency that registers you for your registration history and the date your obligation began. The five-year period runs from your most recent parole, discharge or release, and periods of incarceration or non-compliance do not count.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own conviction record for the registrable offence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting district court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the offence of conviction, the date and the court.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Your own treatment records or provider names
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's treatment providers and agencies
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The petition requires the names of all providers and agencies that have treated you for mental health, substance abuse and offence-related behaviour since the offence. LegalEase records the names you give and never collects or inspects the records themselves.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket fee as provided in K.S.A. 60-2001
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant, paid to the clerk at filing
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the current civil docket fee under K.S.A. 60-2001. Where the expungement petition is combined, its own $176 docket fee applies to that petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The cost of a risk assessment, if the court orders one
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A professional agreed by the parties or approved by the court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only if the court orders a risk assessment under K.S.A. 22-4908(e).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The court may require a risk assessment, performed by a professional agreed upon by the parties or approved by the court, at your own expense.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information or indictment for each charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry showing the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter verifying that the charges were refused
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility basis is that the district attorney declined to prosecute.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that the charges arising out of this arrest were refused. The packet includes a cover request naming exactly which certifications your chosen eligibility basis needs.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the eligibility or fee-exemption basis depends on the absence of pretrial diversion.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the district attorney's office in writing for a letter verifying that you did not participate in a pretrial diversion programme on this arrest. The Article 989 attachment checklist lists it, and the Article 988 fee exemption turns on the same fact.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order of factual innocence and entitlement to compensation under R.S. 15:572.8
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that made the determination
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the eligibility ground is factual innocence under Art. 976(A)(4).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that made the determination for a certified copy.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional. Pursue it only where the agencies will execute one; the track does not depend on it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: This is the agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form, and only they can execute it. If you can obtain one from each named agency and attach them to the motion, the Article 991 Order provides that no contradictory hearing is required and the motion may be granted ex parte. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification verifying no felony convictions during the five-year period and no pending felony charges under a bill of information or indictment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 977(A)(2) five-year route. Not required where the conviction was set aside and dismissed under Article 894(B).
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 977(A)(2) requires this certification to be included with the motion, and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request that names the exact certification and the five-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it — it is the district attorney's own statement about their records — and its absence is a filing requirement, not a reason to withhold the packet.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the Article 894(B) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 977(A)(1) route.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order of dismissal. Where no such order exists and Article 894 relief appears available, obtain it first through the separate Article 987 set-aside track, then return to this one.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information or indictment for each charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry showing the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles under Article 984
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter verifying no participation in a pretrial diversion programme
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the chosen eligibility or fee-exemption basis depends on the absence of pretrial diversion.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Ask the district attorney's office in writing.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Affidavit of No Opposition from each named agency
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney, the Louisiana Bureau of Criminal Identification and Information and the arresting law-enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional; the track does not depend on it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The agencies' own instrument on the Article 990 form. If each named agency executes one and they are attached to the motion, the Article 991 Order provides that no contradictory hearing is required. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Louisiana criminal background check dated within the past sixty days
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana State Police (Right to Review) or the parish sheriff
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Louisiana State Police recommends a fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, original arrest charge, arrest number and counts. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed; the Article 989 form marks it required on its face.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry showing the final disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the case reached a disposition on the court's minutes.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court for the minute entry that shows how each charge was finally disposed of.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information or indictment for each charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where a prosecution was instituted, so a charging instrument exists.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court in the parish of arrest or conviction for a copy of the bill of information or indictment for each charge on the arrest.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Returned Article 988 Motion for Fee Exemption, completed and signed by the district attorney
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) fee exemption.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed. The district attorney or a designee completes the certification boxes and signs, and returns it within fifteen days. Append it to the motion at filing only if you are found eligible. Filing without it means paying the fee, and Article 983 makes the fee non-refundable even if the motion is denied.

The Article 998 motion's prayer asks that where one from each named agency is attached, no contradictory hearing be required and the motion be granted ex parte. LegalEase cannot prepare, complete or sign it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification verifying no conviction of any other criminal offence during the ten-year period and no pending criminal charge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(2) ten-year route and on the Article 978(E) lane.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 978(A)(2) requires it and the Article 989 attachment checklist lists it. Ask the district attorney's office in writing; the packet includes a cover request naming the exact certification and the ten-year window. LegalEase cannot produce it, and its absence is a filing requirement rather than a generation blocker.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the Article 893(E) order setting aside the conviction and dismissing the prosecution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(1) route.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy. Where no such order exists and Article 893 relief appears available, obtain it first on the separate Article 987 track and then return here.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the first offender pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Louisiana Board of Pardons and Committee on Parole, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required on the Article 978(A)(3) first offender pardon route.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Under R.S. 15:572 the pardon is automatic for a first offender on completion of sentence, but it does not issue while court costs for the conviction remain unpaid. If costs are outstanding, pay them and then request the pardon; this is the most common and most fixable obstacle on this route.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Office of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only to a conviction for operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 984 requires a person convicted of operating a vehicle while intoxicated to supplement the motion with a certified letter from the Office of Motor Vehicles proving compliance with that Article, and it is attached to the motion. A further fifty-dollar court cost is assessed and paid to the Office of Motor Vehicles for storage and retrieval.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the order waiving the sex offender registration and notification requirements under R.S. 15:542(F)
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court that issued the waiver
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only to the narrow Article 978(B)(2)(b) carnal-knowledge exception.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Listed on the Article 989 attachment checklist. Article 978(B)(2)(b) makes such an order sufficient to meet the mover's burden of showing that a pre-15-August-2001 carnal knowledge conviction would today be misdemeanour carnal knowledge of a juvenile.

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional, and not available on the Article 978(E) lane, where a contradictory hearing is required by the Article itself.

Louisiana State Police recommends the fingerprint-based Right to Review, because the motion must match the state rap sheet on arrest and booking date, ORIGINAL arrest charge, arrest number and counts — and on this track the original felony arrest charge is the thing being expunged. Order it so it is still inside its sixty-day life on the day the motion is filed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: District attorney certification letter for the underlying entitlement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The district attorney's office for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the underlying entitlement is the Article 977(A)(2) or Article 978(A)(2) route, or where the Article 989 checklist requires a certification for the chosen basis.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Whichever certification the underlying Article 976, 977 or 978 basis requires. The packet's cover request names the exact certification for the basis selected.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Records showing the disposition of each charge on the arrest
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish, or the district attorney's office
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain only if the district attorney's office or the court asks for it when you enquire about an Article 999.1 order.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of court or the district attorney's office for the minute entry or refusal record showing how each charge was disposed of. You will need it to show the court or the district attorney that you meet the Article 999 conditions.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of date of birth
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain only if the district attorney's office or the court asks for it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The age element is the gateway condition, so have proof of your date of birth available when you enquire.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Bill of information for the underlying violation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain where the court or counsel asks for it in connection with an Article 985.3 order.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 985.3(C) requires the served record to include the bill of information. Ask the clerk of court for a copy so it is available when the court considers the order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Sentencing minutes
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain where the court or counsel asks for it in connection with an Article 985.3 order.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 985.3(C) requires the served record to include the sentencing minutes. Ask the clerk of court for a copy.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Documents or records relevant to the arrest incident and any plea agreement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court, the district attorney's office, or the arresting agency
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain where available and where the court or counsel asks for them.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Article 985.3(C) requires these to be included if available.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of successful completion of the probation or alternative sentencing program
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office or the programme administrator
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain where the court or counsel asks for it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Successful completion is the triggering event, so have the discharge or completion document available when you raise Article 985.3 with the court.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Minute entry or sentencing order showing the deferred sentence under Article 893 or Article 894
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain where the court or the district attorney asks to see the basis for the deferral.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the minute entry or sentencing order showing that sentence was deferred and probation imposed under Article 893 or Article 894.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of successful completion of probation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, or the Department of Public Safety and Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain wherever completion may be questioned, which in practice is most cases.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask your probation officer or the supervising office for a discharge or completion letter. The district attorney may contest completion at the contradictory hearing, so have it before the return date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the signed Order of Dismissal, once granted
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of court for the parish of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain after the order is granted, for use on the expungement track that follows.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After the court signs the order of dismissal, ask the clerk for a certified copy. You will need it to move on to the Article 977 or Article 978 expungement track.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Massachusetts Department of Criminal Justice Information Services
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your personal CORI from DCJIS. It shows every court appearance and disposition and is how the controlling most-recent disposition is identified.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a copy of the complaint. The eligibility question turns on the charged amount, which the CORI does not show.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look up the case on Maryland Judiciary Case Search to confirm the court, case number, charges and disposition. Free.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look up the case on Maryland Judiciary Case Search to confirm the court, case number, charges and disposition. Free.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court, or the participant's own financial records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where restitution was ordered in the original proceeding.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the restitution balance. Where it cannot be paid, gather the financial documentation the court will expect at a hearing.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maryland Governor's Office or DPSCS
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of the executed pardon showing the signature date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case record from Maryland Judiciary Case Search
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maryland Judiciary Case Search
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Look up the case on Maryland Judiciary Case Search to confirm the court, case number, charges and disposition. Free.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the judgment and docket record for the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the conviction was entered
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever the offence class or the completion date could be questioned.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court of conviction for a certified copy of the judgment and the docket record. You carry the burden of proving the conviction, its class, and the date you finished the sentence, so bring the paperwork to the hearing. Copy fees apply under the Judicial Branch fee schedule.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maine State Police, State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever the participant is unsure of their full record. Not required by statute or by the form.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own Maine criminal history record so you can see every case the State has on you before you file. It is the reliable way to check the clean-record conditions and to catch a case you had forgotten. A fee applies; confirm the current amount with the Bureau rather than relying on a figure quoted elsewhere.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that every fine and restitution obligation was paid in full
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court of conviction, or the collections office that received payment
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever a fine or restitution balance was part of the sentence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk or the collections office for a payment history or a zero-balance statement. The four-year clock does not start until the last dollar is paid, so this is the document that most often decides the case.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the judgment and docket record for the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the conviction was entered
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever the offence identity could be questioned.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy. On this track the identity of the offence matters more than its class, so the judgment naming Title 17-A former § 853-A is the document to have.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maine State Police, State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended wherever the participant is unsure of their full record. Not required by statute or by the form.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own Maine criminal history record so you can see every case the State has on you before you file. It is the reliable way to check the clean-record conditions and to catch a case you had forgotten. A fee applies; confirm the current amount with the Bureau rather than relying on a figure quoted elsewhere.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maine State Police, State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own Maine criminal history record. On this track it is the whole point: it is the only way to see whether the State is actually carrying the case and whether it is being treated as confidential. Order online through the Bureau's public criminal history request service or by mail to State House Station #42, Augusta, ME 04333-0042. The Bureau charges a fee for the standard record search and a higher fee for a notarised background check; confirm the current amounts with the Bureau before quoting them.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court order or docket entry showing the disposition
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required in practice before the § 709 correction request, because the request has to say what the record should show.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the order or docket entry showing how each charge ended, and specifically whether a dismissal was with or without prejudice. That single word decides the § 703(2) classification.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court docket entry or order showing how the deferred disposition ended
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the docket entry or order showing whether the charge was dismissed under 17-A M.R.S. § 1903 or whether you were convicted of a reduced offence. Participants routinely describe both outcomes as 'it got dismissed', and the two route to completely different places.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the court's written sealing order, or of the pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that signed the sealing order, or the Department of Corrections and the Governor's office for a pardon
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a copy of the signed sealing order, or obtain a copy of the pardon. § 1500-CC(2) makes prompt deletion mandatory where the disputed record is found to be sealed or the subject of a pardon, so this is the document the whole letter turns on. Enclose a copy, never the original.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the official Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Maine State Police, State Bureau of Identification
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Advisable in every case and effectively necessary where the dispute is about accuracy rather than sealing status.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your own Bureau record and enclose a copy. § 1500-CC(1) directs the service to compare its record against the official record maintained by the Bureau, so the Bureau record is the benchmark the statute names. It is strongly advisable wherever the vendor's entry is wrong on facts other than sealing status.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Official documentation of victim status, if the participant already holds any
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The federal, state, tribal or local proceeding that issued it, including a federal immigration proceeding
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Entirely optional. Whether to obtain or present documentation is a strategy decision for the participant's attorney or advocate.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: § 2264(4-A)(B) is explicit that official documentation is NOT required. If it is presented it creates a presumption that participation in the offence was a substantial result of the trafficking or exploitation. Qualifying documentation includes an official record, certification or eligibility letter from a federal, state, tribal or local proceeding, including an approval notice or certification generated in a federal immigration proceeding. Your lawyer or advocate decides whether to present anything; LegalEase never asks you to produce proof and never assesses what you have.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Affidavit or sworn testimony from clergy, a medical professional, victim services staff, or another professional from whom the person sought counsel or assistance
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The professional concerned
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Optional and strategically significant. Not obtained or drafted by LegalEase.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: § 2264(4-A)(C)(2) names this as qualifying documentation. It is prepared by the professional, not by LegalEase and not by the participant, and whether to seek one is a decision for the attorney or advocate.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the judgment and docket record for each conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the conviction was entered
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended so the crime name, date and docket number on the motion match the court record.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy so the motion identifies each conviction correctly. There is no offence restriction on this route, so the judgment is needed for identification rather than for eligibility.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
