participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. Case.net does not show every municipal division, so it is a starting point rather than a complete record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where each case was charged or the finding of guilt entered
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the docket sheet and the judgment or final disposition. A per-page or per-document fee usually applies. This is the document that proves the case number, the court, the offense description and the disposition date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation or parole discharge document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the disposition included probation or parole.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask your former probation or parole officer, or the Division of Probation and Parole, for the discharge document showing the date supervision ended. The waiting period runs from the day you completed the authorized disposition, and for a supervised case that is usually this date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the payment history on each case, showing a zero balance. Paragraph 3 of CR360 has you swear that all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied, including fines and restitution, and an unpaid balance is a common and avoidable reason a petition is dismissed.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal record through MACHS. A name-based search shows open records; a fingerprint-based search is the only way to see records that are already closed, including anything already closed by law under § 610.105. Confirm the current fees with the Patrol before ordering, and note that fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where any case involves a traffic offense, an alcohol-related matter, or a commercial driver licence question.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It shows administrative actions the court file will not, and it is the record that tells you whether a commercial driver licence issue is in play — which is an outright exclusion under § 610.140.3(10).

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record through MACHS. On an arrest that never became a charge this is usually the only document that proves the arrest date, the arresting agency and the offense of arrest, and it is the only search that shows records already closed. Confirm current fees with the Patrol; fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Arrest report or booking record from the arresting agency
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The city police department, county sheriff's department or Highway Patrol troop that made the arrest
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the Highway Patrol record is incomplete or the participant cannot confirm the arrest date or arresting agency from it.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. Under § 610.100 an incident report is generally open; an investigative report may not be. Fees vary by agency.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net search confirming no case was opened
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net by your name and name variants in the arrest county and any county where a charge might have been filed. What you are looking for is the absence of a case. If a case exists, this is the wrong route and you belong on the conviction route or on the § 610.122 route.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and the judgment or order of dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court in which the case originated
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the originating court for a certified copy of the docket and of the judgment or order. § 610.105.1 keeps the judgment or order a public record even after the rest of the file closes, so the clerk can supply it. This is the document that tells you which of the four dispositions you actually have.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net for your name and name variants in the county where the case was filed, and print or screenshot what you find, including the date you looked.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. A name-based search shows only open records, so it cannot tell you whether a case closed — it can only fail to show it. A fingerprint-based search returns closed and complete records for the requesting individual and is the only way to confirm that closure actually happened at the central repository. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation discharge document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the disposition was a suspended imposition of sentence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Division of Probation and Parole or the supervising court for the discharge document. Final termination for a suspended imposition of sentence means probation has ended, and this is the document that proves the date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Three standard fingerprint cards
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Arrest report or booking record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting law enforcement agency
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. It supplies the date of arrest, the citation number, the offense charged and the agency name, all of which § 610.123 makes mandatory contents of the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the charge was filed
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where a charge was filed and the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the entry disposing of each offense related to the arrest. The ground requires that every related offense or violation was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, so the participant needs the disposition for each one, not just the lead charge.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is how the participant builds the agency list and confirms the prior-and-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant is relying on the chapter 303 or moving-violation ground, or where commercial driver licence status is in any doubt.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record. It shows the offense classification and whether a commercial driver licence was ever issued, and commercial licence status at the time of arrest is an outright bar on the moving-violation ground.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It is the document that shows administrative suspensions and revocations under §§ 302.500 to 302.540 and chemical-test refusals, which are alcohol-related enforcement contacts under § 302.525.3 even where no conviction followed. A participant who answers the enforcement-contact question from memory will very often be wrong.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Out-of-state driver records
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The licensing authority of each other state where the participant has held a licence
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence in any state other than Missouri.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state, and § 610.130.4 bars anyone issued or required to hold a commercial driver's licence in any state.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment from the court of plea or sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the municipal, associate circuit or circuit court that took the plea or imposed the sentence
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It establishes the plea or sentencing date the ten-year period runs from, the offense level, and the case number.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your own criminal record. It supports the agency list and the no-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout for each marijuana case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net for your name and name variants in the county where each case was charged, and print what you find with the date you looked. A case that has been expunged will usually have disappeared from public view, so an absence is evidence — but not proof, because Case.net does not cover every municipal division.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is the only search that shows records already closed, so it is the one that can tell you whether Article XIV relief was already entered. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was charged or the finding of guilt entered
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It supplies the case number, the court, the offense grade and the charge description, and on a marijuana case it is often the only place the quantity appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certificate of expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered the expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where expungement has already been ordered, or after an order is entered on the participant's own petition.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for the certificate of expungement. Article XIV, section 2 requires the court to issue a certificate stating that the offense has been expunged. Ask what the fee is and how long it takes. This is the document to keep.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and the entry dismissing the charge or the not-guilty judgment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the charge was last pending
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and of the entry disposing of the charge. It establishes which of the two routes applies, and if an expungement order was already entered under § 610.145.1(2) the docket is where you will see it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the identity was used without permission, or that a misidentification occurred
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own records, the arresting agency, the prosecuting attorney, or a police identity-theft report
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Gather whatever shows the case was not yours: a police report naming another person, an identity-theft report you filed, correspondence from the prosecutor, a court entry recording the mistake, employment or travel records placing you elsewhere. LegalEase never sees, holds or assesses this; the court decides whether it is enough.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the matter affected the participant's driving licence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record. It shows the points, suspension or revocation the order will require the Department to reverse, and it is what you will check afterwards to confirm they did.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. On an identity case this does double duty: it shows what is recorded against you, and because the search is by fingerprint rather than by name it is the record least likely to be carrying someone else's conduct under your name.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Three standard fingerprint cards
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court filing, whether they can do three in one visit, the cost, the payment method and what identification to bring. § 610.123.1(7) makes the card a content of the petition, and CR300 recites that you are providing them for verification of your identity. One card goes to the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, one is yours.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. This is the single most important document on this route: a name-based search will return the impersonator's conduct under your name, and a fingerprint-based search will not, so the difference between the two is itself evidence of what happened. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: The arrest report or court file showing the record that falsely identifies the participant
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting agency, or the clerk of the court where the case was filed
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the arrest record from the arresting agency and the docket from the clerk. You need to see exactly which of your identifying details were recorded, because the court's finding is about how many of your identifying factors were falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Police report or Federal Trade Commission identity-theft report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Local law enforcement, or identitytheft.gov
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has reported the identity theft, or is advised to.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: File a report with local police and, separately, an identity-theft report with the Federal Trade Commission at identitytheft.gov. Neither is required by § 575.120.4, but both are ordinary corroboration and the Federal Trade Commission report is what you will need for the credit bureaus, which a Missouri court order does not reach.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment from the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that imposed the sentence
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It establishes the statute of conviction — which must be § 311.325 rather than a local ordinance — the sentencing date and the case number.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record. It is where an administrative alcohol-related suspension or revocation appears, and § 302.525.3 makes any such action an enforcement contact that disqualifies you under § 311.326 even though it was never a criminal conviction. A participant answering this question from memory of court cases will very often be wrong.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Out-of-state driver records
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The licensing authority of each other state where the participant has held a licence
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the participant has held a driving licence outside Missouri.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your own criminal record. It supports the agency list and the no-other-alcohol-related-offense condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is the record the central repository's own analysis runs on, and a fingerprint-based search is the only one that shows records already closed — so after the section becomes operative it is the only way to see whether your offense was expunged. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for the drug case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It shows the statute of conviction, which decides whether the offense is one of the four the law reaches, and whether the case contained any other conviction — which takes the whole case out if it did.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Probation or parole discharge document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Where the sentence included probation or parole.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask for the discharge document. Final disposition under § 610.141 means completion of all court-imposed terms and conditions and unconditional release from custody, so this is the document that fixes the date the clock runs from.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Case.net printout for the drug case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search Case.net for the case. Once the section is operating, the Office of the State Courts Administrator expunges the corresponding case records in the statewide court automation system, so a case that has disappeared from Case.net may have been reached — though the Highway Patrol record is the better check.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the disposition or sentencing order from the clerk
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was heard
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that heard your case for a certified copy of the order showing how the case ended. Mississippi has no central portal and each clerk holds their own file, so identify the right court first.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the indictment
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Circuit clerk of the county
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies only where a grand jury returned an indictment.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order placing you on nonadjudication and setting the conditions.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the DUI judgment of conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that entered the DUI conviction for a certified copy of the judgment.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Blood or breath test result, or documentation that no test was refused
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The arresting agency, the court file, or the Mississippi Crime Laboratory
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the test result. The statute conditions relief on not having refused the test and, where results are available, on a concentration below .16, so this document is central rather than optional.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified driving record
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Mississippi Department of Public Safety
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your certified driving record. It establishes whether any other DUI appears and whether you held a commercial licence.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the administering court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that ran the programme for a certified copy of the order recording your successful completion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the final disposition, and of any dismissal or expungement order already entered
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the administering court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk what the final disposition was and whether any order dismissing or expunging the case has already been entered. On an intervention court case that copy may be all you need.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Mississippi criminal history record

participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Advisable on every track and effectively necessary wherever first-offender status or a multi-court good-conduct period is in issue.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own Mississippi criminal history so you can see every case on your record before you file. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status or good conduct across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order deferring proceedings and placing you on probation without an adjudication of guilt.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the order of discharge and dismissal
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order discharging you and dismissing the proceedings.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof of successful completion of probation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising authority or the clerk
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the documentation showing you completed probation and every condition.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own Mississippi criminal history so you can see every case on your record before you file. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status or good conduct across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order showing how the case ended.

participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Advisable wherever a fine was imposed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for confirmation that any fine and costs are paid in full.

participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain your own Mississippi criminal history so you can see every case on your record before you file. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status or good conduct across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

participantFilingRequirements.name: DOJ CRISS criminal background check
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Department of Justice, Criminal Records Information Services Section
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Montana criminal background check from DOJ CRISS, available online, by mail or in person. The judiciary packet estimates roughly $10 to $30. You need it to build a complete conviction list, and the petition is once in a lifetime.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Montana Public Access Portal searches — District Courts AND Courts of Limited Jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Judicial Branch public access portals
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run TWO separate searches, one on the District Courts portal and one on the Courts of Limited Jurisdiction portal, under SEARCHES, then Case Searches, then By Party. This is not optional: the judiciary packet warns that some misdemeanour convictions do not appear on the CRISS background check, and Montana has no centralised court records system.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the final judgment from each convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of each convicting court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each court that entered a conviction for a copy of the final judgment. A per-document fee may apply. Obtain certified copies for the DOJ stage.

participantFilingRequirements.name: FD-258 blue applicant fingerprint card, with prints taken
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Card free from Montana DOJ CRISS; prints taken by local law enforcement or a private vendor
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the free FD-258 blue applicant fingerprint card from DOJ CRISS and have your prints taken by local law enforcement or a private company, expecting a fee for the printing. Section 46-18-1104(3) requires fingerprinting to validate identity and the CRISS form requires the card. Start this early: it is a physical-world dependency that people discover too late. It is needed before you mail the CRISS request, NOT before your court packet is prepared.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the district court expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court that granted the petition
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtained after the court order issues, for the DOJ stage.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After the court grants the petition, ask the clerk for a certified copy of the expungement order. You need it for the CRISS submission and for the copies you send to the arresting agency, the prosecutor and the clerk of each convicting court.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Filing fee, or a statement of inability to pay court costs and fees
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district court; the fee-waiver form is published by Montana Legal Services Association
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The Montana Clerks of District Courts civil fee schedule, updated May 2024, sets $120 for civil commencement of an action by a petitioner. If you cannot pay, the judiciary and MLSA route you to the interactive Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees on montanalawhelp.org, with a proposed order. LegalEase links you to that published form and does not reproduce it, because it carries a non-commercial-use restriction.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of your criminal record from the Montana Department of Justice
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Department of Justice, Criminal Records Information Services Section
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order your Montana criminal record from DOJ. Form B marks it as a required attachment to the petition. Roughly $10 to $30.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the judgment or sentencing order for the conviction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Recommended by OCA for the petition and needed for the DOJ stage after an expungement order.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a copy. The OCA form marks it recommended rather than required, and you will need the original or a certified copy later for the DOJ stage if expungement is granted.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the court order of expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtained after an expungement order, for the DOJ stage. Not applicable on a redesignation outcome.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After the court grants expungement, ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order. It is enclosed with the CRISS request.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Filing fee for the sentencing court's level, or a statement of inability to pay court costs and fees
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court; the fee-waiver form is published by Montana Legal Services Association
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The fee depends on the court level. In District Court the civil commencement fee is $120 per the Clerks of District Courts schedule; Justice, Municipal and City Court fees differ and are not resolved, so ask the clerk. If you cannot pay, the OCA instructions route you to the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees on montanalawhelp.org. LegalEase links you to that published form and does not reproduce it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of your criminal record from the Montana Department of Justice
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Department of Justice, Criminal Records Information Services Section
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Form A marks the DOJ criminal record as a required attachment. If you are in custody, ask your attorney, a family member or the facility's law library about how to request it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court documents for the conviction and the current sentence
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the judgment and the sentencing order. If you are in custody, your attorney or a family member may need to obtain them for you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified copy of the court order of expungement
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtained after an expungement order only. Not applicable on a resentencing outcome.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After an expungement order, ask the clerk for a certified copy. It is enclosed with the CRISS request.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Filing fee for the sentencing court's level, or a statement of inability to pay court costs and fees
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court; the fee-waiver form is published by Montana Legal Services Association
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The fee depends on the court level; ask the clerk. If you cannot pay, the OCA instructions route you to the Statement of Inability to Pay Court Costs and Fees on montanalawhelp.org, which LegalEase links to and does not reproduce.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the deferred sentence order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a copy of the deferred sentence order. It gives you the case number and the deferral period, and you will need it again at the DOJ stage.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Confirmation from the court record that no petition to revoke was filed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk to confirm from the case file whether a petition to revoke was ever filed during the deferral period. On a felony this is dispositive: § 46-18-204(1)(a) makes dismissal mandatory only where no revocation petition was filed. LegalEase will not assert this for you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the dismissal order once granted
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtained after the order issues, for the DOJ stage.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: After the court signs the order, ask the clerk for a copy. It is enclosed with the CRISS request together with the deferred sentence order.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Documentation of compliance with the deferral conditions
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising probation office, the treatment provider, or the clerk's payment records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Obtain only where the court or the prosecuting office questions completion.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Where the court asks for proof that you completed the conditions, obtain the discharge or payment records that show it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Montana public criminal history record check via CHOPRS or by mail
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Department of Justice, Criminal Records Information Services Section
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: DOJ instructs you to run this BEFORE submitting the request, so you know what the record actually shows. Allow for a hold of up to seventy-two hours on a CHOPRS request. A fee applies, roughly $10 to $30.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court judgment or disposition document
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that handled the case
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The 2024 form lists the court judgment for this request type. Ask the clerk for the judgment or the disposition order showing how each charge ended.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Legible photocopy of valid photo identification
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The participant's own state-issued identification card, driver's licence or passport
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: The 2023 version of the form required photo identification for a Non-Conviction Removal request and the 2024 version does not list it. Because the two disagree, include it by default; it costs nothing and avoids a refused request.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court documentation of the outcome, where the DOJ record is incomplete
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court of jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Applies where the DOJ record is incomplete because the court did not report the disposition.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Where the DOJ record is incomplete rather than wrong, CRISS will attempt to obtain the outcome from the court. If it cannot, you will need to contact the court and ask it to send the final outcome to the Montana Department of Justice.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Montana public criminal history record check via CHOPRS or by mail
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Department of Justice, Criminal Records Information Services Section
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Run the check to see whether the automatic removal has already happened. Allow for a hold of up to seventy-two hours on a CHOPRS request. A fee of roughly $10 to $30 applies.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Montana Public Access Portal search results — District Courts AND Courts of Limited Jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Montana Judicial Branch public access portals
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Search both portals under SEARCHES, then Case Searches, then By Party. Montana has no centralised court records system, and the court record is a separate question from the DOJ record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Court documentation of the final outcome
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The court of jurisdiction
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Needed only where the automatic removal did not occur.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Where the non-conviction still appears on the DOJ record, contact the court of jurisdiction and ask it to send the final outcome to the Montana Department of Justice. The court's failure to report is the usual reason the automatic removal did not happen.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police. Rule 790 requires a current copy obtained within 60 days before filing to be attached, unless the attorney for the Commonwealth agrees to waive it. Because of the 60-day window, order it late in packet assembly rather than first. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Complete docket sheet for the case
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet showing every charge, the OTN, and the disposition of each count.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police. Rule 490 requires a current copy obtained within 60 days before filing to be attached. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Magisterial district court docket sheet
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The magisterial district court, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet showing every charge and its disposition, and confirm no misdemeanour or felony was filed with the summary offences.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet showing the verdict on every count
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet and confirm a not-guilty verdict on every count arising from the incident. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Used to verify whether the record actually cleared once twelve months have passed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report to check whether the acquitted cycle still appears.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Docket sheet showing the ARD dismissal and any expungement order
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet and check whether an expungement order was entered with the dismissal. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Records showing final release from confinement or supervision
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The supervising county probation department or the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only on the age-70 ground, to establish when the ten-year clock began.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising agency for confirmation of the final release date.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Certified death certificate
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Department of Health, Division of Vital Records
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only on the deceased ground.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Order a certified death certificate from Vital Records.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Proof that the driving-privilege suspension was completed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Only where a licence suspension was imposed for the offence.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request a driver history from PennDOT showing the suspension was served and restoration completed. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Copy of the pardon
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania Board of Pardons
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain a copy of the pardon showing whether it was unconditional. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.conditionDescription: Required only where the fallback Rule 790 petition is filed.
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request the criminal history report within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police within 60 days before filing and attach it to the petition, unless the attorney for the Commonwealth agrees to waive it. Because of the 60-day window, order it late in packet assembly. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Complete docket sheet showing every charge on the docket and the sentence imposed
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of courts, or the Unified Judicial System web docket sheets
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Obtain the docket sheet showing every count, the grading, the sentence imposed and the restitution status.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Pennsylvania State Police
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history report to see whether the record has been given limited access. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.
